questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between ionising power and penetrating power of radiation?

options.text: The more ionising, the more penetrating
The more ionising, the less penetrating
Ionising power and penetrating power are unrelated
All types of radiation have equal ionising and penetrating power

questions.explanation: There is an inverse relationship: the more ionising the radiation, the less penetrating it is. Alpha radiation is the most ionising but least penetrating because it uses up its energy quickly by ionising nearby atoms. Gamma radiation is the least ionising but most penetrating because it interacts weakly with matter.

questions.stem: What is the source of energy released in both fission and fusion reactions?

options.text: A small amount of mass is converted to energy according to E = mc squared
The kinetic energy of the neutrons

questions.explanation: In both fission and fusion, the total mass of the products is slightly less than the total mass of the reactants. This 'missing' mass (called the mass defect) has been converted into energy according to Einstein's equation E = mc squared. Because the speed of light squared is an enormous number, even a tiny mass loss releases a huge amount of energy.
